message.content: {"back_translation":"It was on a murky November night that I beheld the completion of my exertions. With an anxiety that almost bordered on torment, I gathered the instruments of life around me, so that I might pour a spark of being into the lifeless thing that lay at my feet. It was already one o'clock in the morning; the rain drummed gloomily against the panes, and my candle was almost burnt down, when, by the glimmer of the half-extinguished light, I saw how the murky, yellow eye of the creature opened; it breathed heavily, and a convulsive movement twitched through its limbs.\n\nHow am I able to describe my feelings at this catastrophe, or how to draw the wretched one whom I had tried to form with such endless exertions and such carefulness? His limbs were well proportioned, and I had picked out his features as beautiful. Beautiful! – Great God! His yellow skin barely covered the web of muscles and arteries lying beneath; his hair was of a shining black and billowing; his teeth of pearl-like whiteness; but these splendours formed only an all the more gruesome contrast to his watery eyes, which seemed almost of the same colour as the pale-white cavities in which they sat, his shrivelled complexion and the straight, black lips.","changes":[{"shelley":"these luxuriances","translation":"diese Herrlichkeiten","back_translation":"these splendours / glories","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"\"Luxuriances\" suggests excessive, overgrown abundance, whereas \"Herrlichkeiten\" praises the features as magnificent, which weakens the sense of excess."},{"shelley":"the work of muscles and arteries beneath","translation":"das darunterliegende Geflecht von Muskeln und Arterien","back_translation":"the web/network of muscles and arteries lying beneath","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"\"Work\" (the machinery or workings of the body, with an echo of the maker's labour) becomes a static woven \"Geflecht\", so the image changes and the artisanal overtone is lost."},{"shelley":"the rain pattered dismally against the panes","translation":"der Regen prasselte düster gegen die Scheiben","back_translation":"the rain drummed/crackled gloomily against the panes","category":"intensification","rationale":"\"Prasseln\" is a harder, noisier verb than \"pattered\", though \"düster\" for \"dismally\" is close."},{"shelley":"a convulsive motion agitated its limbs","translation":"eine krampfhafte Bewegung durchzuckte ihre Glieder","back_translation":"a convulsive movement twitched/flashed through its limbs","category":"intensification","rationale":"\"Durchzucken\" is more sudden and vivid than \"agitated\", although this is a mild difference."},{"shelley":"the dull yellow eye","translation":"das trübe, gelbe Auge","back_translation":"the murky/cloudy, yellow eye","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"\"Trüb\" suggests cloudiness or turbidity rather than dullness, and it repeats the word used for \"dreary\" in the first sentence, so the two English adjectives are no longer distinguished."},{"shelley":"the dun white sockets","translation":"den fahlweißen Höhlen","back_translation":"the pale-white cavities","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"\"Dun\" (a dull greyish-brown tint) becomes \"fahl\" (pallid), and \"Höhlen\" (cavities, caves) is more cave-like than \"sockets\", so the colour and the image both change slightly."},{"shelley":"his hair was of a lustrous black, and flowing","translation":"sein Haar war von glänzendem Schwarz und wallend","back_translation":"his hair was of a shining black and billowing","category":"intensification","rationale":"\"Wallend\" is more poetic and billowy than plain \"flowing\", which makes the beauty a little more lavish."},{"shelley":"that I might infuse a spark of being","translation":"auf dass ich ... einflößen möge","back_translation":"so that I might pour in","category":"domestication","rationale":"The archaic, biblical-sounding \"auf dass ... möge\" gives a solemn register that matches German literary convention more than Shelley's plainer purpose clause, though it could also count as intensification."},{"shelley":"with such infinite pains and care","translation":"mit so unendlichen Mühen und solcher Sorgfalt","back_translation":"with such endless exertions and such carefulness","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"\"Mühen\" renders both \"toils\" in the first sentence and \"pains\" here, so the repetition flattens a distinction in Shelley's vocabulary of labour."}],"note":"The translation is close and sentence-by-sentence faithful, with no real omissions or additions. Its tendencies are a slightly elevated, literary German register (\"auf dass ... möge\", \"vermag\", \"wallend\") and a handful of lexical choices that soften or reshape Shelley's images, most notably \"Herrlichkeiten\" for \"luxuriances\" and \"Geflecht\" for \"work\". These shifts are small, and a few (such as \"trübe\" appearing twice) may reflect limited German vocabulary rather than deliberate choice."}
